title: The Margin Erosion That Started in July and Is Only Showing Up Now
linkedin:
Revenue looks fine this September. Margin is a notch thinner than it should be, and nothing this month explains why.

The usual answer is two months old. On 1 July, award wages stepped up, insurance renewals landed, key suppliers reset their price lists, and CPI-linked leases adjusted for the new financial year. None of it hit straight away, because work quoted in May and June was still being delivered through July and August at the old numbers.

Most businesses don't compare a July cost base against a July price list. They compare this month's revenue to this month's costs, see a result in the usual range, and move on.

By September, the last of the old-priced work has cleared the pipeline. What's left is the new cost base sitting against pricing that hasn't moved, which is exactly what shows up as a quieter margin with no obvious cause.

For businesses with longer sales or project cycles, construction and professional services especially, this isn't a one-off correction. It's a slow bleed that keeps showing for another quarter or two after the cost increases land, compounding every week the old pricing stays live.

The fix isn't complicated. It's rebuilding the cost base, checking it against current pricing line by line, and having the pricing conversation that got deferred back in June because it felt awkward at the time.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog. Link in the first comment.
